defects.claim_says: 1-101 (the restatement of section 1-101 of EO 12201) was 'exhausted by performance on 1980-07-28'; the amended text and its October 31, 1980 revocation are 'consequences of the performed amendment, not continuing commands of this order'; whole_order_end 1980-08-11
defects.source_says: The text this order wrote into section 1-101 of EO 12201 authorizes the Board of Governors to set uniform requirements 'provided however, such authorization is revoked as of October 31,1980', so it keeps operating through October 31, 1980. Under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (strike-and-insert), as this batch applies it to EO 10084-10174, 12376, 12447, 12187 and 12584, a restating amendment continues, amended, until the parent ends; it is not spent when it takes effect. On that reading the 1-101 clause runs at least to 1980-10-31, which is later than the recorded whole-order end of 1980-08-11.

defects.claim_says: Terminated 1980-07-28 'exhausted by performance', while the same reason says 'the amended definition survives as part of Executive Order No. 12201'
defects.source_says: No held instrument ends EO 12201 as a whole: cruden finds it cited only in EO 12225's own printings, and EO 12553 does not list it. The definition this order wrote can therefore end no earlier than the last of the EO 12201 authorizations it serves, which by the amended section 1-101 is October 31, 1980. The claim gives no evidence that it ended on 1980-07-28.

reasoning: The corrected 1980 dates match the held text, and the three revocations (1-102 as of 1980-08-11, 1-103 as of 1980-07-28, 1-105 on signing 1980-07-03) are correctly treated as performed acts. The two restating amendments (1-101 and 1-104), however, are treated as spent on their July 28, 1980 effective date. That conflicts with the strike-and-insert reading applied to the other amending orders in this batch, and it conflicts with the order's own text, which keeps the restated authorization alive until October 31, 1980. The whole-order end of 1980-08-11 is therefore not supported as the latest first end. A consistent claim would date the 1-101 end at least 1980-10-31, give 1-104 an evidenced end, and recompute whole_order_end. Alternatively it could adopt the spent-on-performance reading for amendments, but only with an explicit reason why that reading governs here and not in the other orders of this batch.
